case_timeout_sec_note: Wall-clock budget per case, generation through execution. Calibrated 2026-08-19 from the 4056 pre-cap wave-1 records: p50=36.0 p90=85.9 p95=103.7 p99=157.8 max=377.0 sec. 600 is ~1.6x the observed maximum and ~3.8x p99, and sits above ocpq_cli_timeout_sec (300) so the backend's own timeout still fires first for a pure execution hang. It is therefore a bound on pathology, not a budget that trims the normal distribution: no observed case came within 220s of it. A cap tight enough to actually bind would have to sit below 300 and would make the CLI timeout unreachable.
max_result_file_gb_note: Refuse to parse a prediction's result export larger than this. Parsing loads the whole file at once, so an over-selecting query SIGKILLs the shard -- uncatchable. MEASURED 2026-08-27 (src/diagnose_result_size.py, job 3233233) by replaying the failing query with no model: the export is 6.283 GB and could not be parsed in 122 GB, so the multiplier for this data shape is >19.4x, not the 11.7x measured on gold-shaped exports. At 19.4x a 64 GB shard could parse at most ~3.3 GB, so a 4 GB cap sits ABOVE anything the other 95 shards could have handled and is provably inert for them; a 4 GB file needs ~78 GB, which exceeds their 64 GB but fits the 122 GB rerun. Inertness would only break below 16x. Set this from measurement, not from a multiplier -- every export above 256 MB now logs its true size before the read.
